content.title: About
content.content: Pancakes are a classic dish made from a thin batter of flour, milk, eggs, and a touch of sugar. The batter cooks quickly on a hot skillet, forming soft, slightly crisp layers. Pancakes are commonly served with sour cream, honey, berries, cottage cheese, or savory fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes are known in over 30 countries under different names: crepes (France), blini (Russia), okonomiyaki (Japan).
The tradition of eating pancakes on Maslenitsa in Russia marks the farewell to winter and the arrival of spring.
The world’s largest pancake was made in 2012 in the USA: 15.5 m in diameter and weighing 2.5 t.
Japanese “millet” pancakes are made from rice flour and are gluten‑free.
Pancakes are a frequent contest item because of their versatility and quick preparation.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pancakes provide a fast‑acting energy source thanks to the carbs in the batter.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and milk supply a complete set of essential amino acids.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain flour adds B1, B2 and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Dairy ingredients support bone and tooth health.

items.title: Low fat when lightly cooked
items.content: Using minimal oil keeps pancakes suitable for a balanced diet.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional wheat flour can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet toppings and added sugar increase the calorie load.

items.title: Frying in oil
items.content: Excessive oil adds saturated fat and calories.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Milk in the batter may be problematic for those who cannot digest lactose.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve pancakes hot, rolled or folded. They can be brushed with butter, drizzled with honey, jam, or topped with cottage cheese, or filled with meat, fish, or vegetables. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain or gluten‑free flour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them on parchment sheets in bags and reheat in the microwave or skillet.
